members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a causal language model with context-aware prompt tuning.
members.extended:
CPT (Blau et al., 2024, [arXiv:2410.17222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17222)) tunes a prompt made of in-context examples: the
prompt's tokens start as the embeddings of `cpt_token_ids` and a trainable *delta* is
added to each.  Each token has a type (`cpt_tokens_type_mask`, read modulo 4: `1` an input
template, `2` an input, `3` an output template, `0` or `4` an output or padding) that
says which deltas train (types 1-3 only) and how far a delta may move: after every step its
norm is projected back onto a ball of radius `opt_projection_epsilon` (inputs) or
`opt_projection_format_epsilon` (templates), scaled by $\sqrt{d/2048}$.  The loss
covers the output tokens of the prompt and of the batch, optionally down-weighted for earlier
examples (`opt_weighted_loss_type="decay"`).

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference adapter library's.  `num_virtual_tokens` is `len(cpt_token_ids)` whatever is passed.

parameters.name: cpt_token_ids
parameters.description: The vocabulary ids whose embeddings the prompt starts from; `[0]` by default.

parameters.name: cpt_mask
parameters.description: One entry per token (kept for the file's sake); ones by default.

parameters.name: cpt_tokens_type_mask
parameters.description: One type per token, as above; ones by default.

parameters.name: opt_weighted_loss_type
parameters.description:
`"decay"` weights the loss of each earlier output segment of an example by a further
factor of `opt_loss_decay_factor`.

parameters.name: opt_projection_epsilon
parameters.description: Radius of the ball a delta of an input token stays in.

parameters.name: opt_projection_format_epsilon
parameters.description: Radius for the deltas of template tokens.

parameters.name: tokenizer_name_or_path
parameters.description: Kept for the file's sake; the prompt's tokens are given as ids.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
`task_type` is not `"CAUSAL_LM"`, or the three per-token lists differ in length.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import CPTConfig
>>> config = CPTConfig(cpt_token_ids=[5, 6, 7], cpt_tokens_type_mask=[1, 2, 4], task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
>>> config.num_virtual_tokens, config.cpt_mask
(3, [1, 1, 1])
>>> CPTConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

members.summary: The prompt of CPT: frozen token embeddings plus a trainable delta kept near zero.
members.extended:
Built to train it holds `embedding` (the model's embeddings of `cpt_token_ids`, frozen)
and `delta_embedding` (zeros).  Each call first projects every delta row onto the ball of
radius $\epsilon_t$ — the input or template epsilon of its token type, times
$\sqrt{d/2048}$ — writing the result back into the parameter (the optimiser steps from
the projected value, as the reference's does), then returns `embedding + delta`.  Only the
deltas of types 1 to 3 (templates and inputs) receive a gradient.  Built for
`inference_mode` it holds `embedding` alone, whose rows are the finished prompt.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The token ids and types, the epsilons, and `token_dim` set.

parameters.name: word_embeddings
parameters.description: The model's token table; its rows for `cpt_token_ids` start the prompt.

raises.description: A trainable prompt is built from a table that is not an `nn.Embedding`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import CPTConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.cpt import CPTEmbedding
>>> config = CPTConfig(cpt_token_ids=[1, 2], cpt_tokens_type_mask=[2, 4], token_dim=8,
...                    task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
>>> prompt = CPTEmbedding(config, nn.Embedding(5, 8))
>>> prompt(lucid.arange(2).long()).shape
(2, 8)
>>> [p.requires_grad for p in prompt.parameters()]
[False, True]

methods.name: get_model_config
methods.summary: `model`'s config as a dict, whatever it is held as.
methods.extended:
A config with a `to_dict` method is converted by it, a dataclass by `asdict`, a
mapping is copied.  A model with no `config` (or one that is `None`) has the
reference's stand-in, `{"model_type": "custom"}`, which is what the default target
modules and the prompt geometry read for a model of no known type.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to read the config of.

returns.description: The config's entries; a new dict, whose changes do not reach the model.

raises.description: `model.config` is none of a mapping, a dataclass or an object with `to_dict`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraModel
>>> LoraModel.get_model_config(nn.Linear(2, 2))
{'model_type': 'custom'}

members.summary: The tuner of context-aware prompt tuning: a `CPTEmbedding` per adapter, in front of the input.
members.extended:
The prompt goes in front of the input embeddings as in prompt tuning.  A call that passes
`labels` is the one that differs: the model is run without them, and the loss is CPT's — the
next-token cross-entropy over the *output* tokens of the prompt followed by the input, as the
type mask marks them, averaged and optionally decayed (`CPTConfig`).  `input_type_mask`
(`(batch, tokens)` integers, all outputs when omitted) gives the types of the input's
tokens; give `labels` and `input_type_mask` as keywords.  A call without labels, and
`generate`, are prompt tuning's.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The causal language model to prompt.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models import create_model
>>> from lucid.peft import CPTConfig, CPTModel
>>> lm = create_model("gpt2_small_lm", vocab_size=32, hidden_size=16, num_hidden_layers=1,
...                   num_attention_heads=2, intermediate_size=32, max_position_embeddings=16)
>>> tuned = CPTModel(lm, CPTConfig(cpt_token_ids=[3, 4, 5], cpt_tokens_type_mask=[1, 2, 4],
...                                task_type="CAUSAL_LM"))
>>> ids = lucid.randint(0, 32, (2, 5))
>>> tuned(ids, labels=ids).logits.shape   # the prompt's 3 positions come first
(2, 8, 32)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.cpt` — context-aware prompt tuning: a prompt of in-context examples with a bounded learned offset.
extended:
CPT (Blau et al., 2024, [arXiv:2410.17222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17222)) tunes a prompt that is itself a few in-context examples.
Its tokens start as the embeddings of `cpt_token_ids` and each gets a trainable delta, held near
zero by a projection after every step (templates and inputs may move, outputs may not), so the
examples keep their meaning while the prompt adapts.  The loss counts the output tokens of the
prompt as well as of the batch, optionally weighting earlier examples less.  Pick it for few-shot
fine-tuning of a causal language model when the examples should stay in context; for a free
prompt that starts anywhere, use prompt tuning.

Like the other prompt methods it adds no layer: the prompt is put in front of the input by hooks
on the model's call, so `model(...)` and `generate` both carry it, and the adapter file holds
the finished prompt as `prompt_embeddings`.  `CPTConfig` and `CPTModel` are here and exported
from `lucid.peft`; `CPTEmbedding` is the learned part.  Importing the package registers the
method under `PeftType.CPT`.
citation: Blau, Tsachi, et al. "Context-Aware Prompt Tuning: Advancing In-Context Learning with Adversarial Methods." [arXiv:2410.17222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17222), 2024.
